source.titleEnglishInternal: Settle who pays for the group
source.objectiveEnglishInternal: offer to pay, respond when others insist, and follow local custom on treating
source.roleplayEnglishInternal: Your new friends insist on paying for breakfast; negotiate politely, accept or decline, and agree how to settle.

readerVerbExamples.target: Si ustedes pagan la cuenta, yo dejo la propina.
readerVerbExamples.native: If you pay the bill, I'll leave the tip.

readerVerbExamples.target: Mis amigos insisten en pagar el desayuno.
readerVerbExamples.native: My friends insist on paying for breakfast.
Shall we split the bill among all of us?

archivedDraft.scene: Friends finish breakfast and politely agree on the bill.

sourceCards.sourceNoteInternal: Ask for it with: La cuenta, por favor.
Common in Mexico; in Spain you hear camarero.
Mexican pastries like conchas, usually eaten with coffee.
Invitar means to treat someone; whoever says yo invito pays.
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: 今日の朝ごはんは、わたしのおごりです。
いいえ、本当に、わたしに払わせてください。

sourceCards.sourceSpanish: Bueno, gracias, pero la próxima vez invito yo.
sourceCards.sourceEnglish: OK, thanks, but next time it's on me.
sourceCards.sourceNoteInternal: A polite way to accept when friends insist.
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: じゃあ、ありがとうございます。でも次は、わたしがおごります。
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: OK, thanks, but next time it's on me.

sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: それなら、わたしがチップを置きます。

sourceCards.sourceEnglish: Is it customary to leave a tip here?
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: ここでは、チップを置く習慣がありますか？
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Is it customary to leave a tip here?

sourceCards.sourceEnglish: Shall we split the bill among all of us?
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: 会計はみんなで割り勘にしましょうか？
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Shall we split the bill among all of us?

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Después de un desayuno con café y pan dulce en Oaxaca, el mesero trae la cuenta a nuestra mesa.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: After a breakfast of coffee and sweet bread in Oaxaca, the waiter brings the bill to our table.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: オアハカで、コーヒーと菓子パンの朝ごはんを食べたあと、ウェイターがわたしたちのテーブルに伝票を持ってきます。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: After a breakfast of coffee and sweet bread in Oaxaca, the waiter brings the bill to our table.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Yo saco mi tarjeta y digo: Yo invito el desayuno hoy, porque ustedes me enseñaron la ciudad.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: I take out my card and say: Breakfast is on me today, because you showed me the city.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: わたしはカードを取り出して言います。「今日の朝ごはんは、わたしのおごりです。ふたりがこの街を案内してくれたから。」
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: I take out my card and say: Breakfast is on me today, because you showed me the city.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Mis nuevos amigos, Lucía y Andrés, insisten: No, aquí tú eres nuestro invitado.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: My new friends, Lucía and Andrés, insist: No, here you are our guest.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 新しい友達のルシアとアンドレスは、こう言ってゆずりません。「いいえ、ここではあなたがわたしたちのゲストです。」
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: My new friends, Lucía and Andrés, insist: No, here you are our guest.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Les digo: No, de veras, déjenme pagar, pero Andrés ya le da efectivo al mesero.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: I tell them: No, really, let me pay, but Andrés is already giving cash to the waiter.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 「いいえ、本当に、わたしに払わせてください」とふたりに言いますが、アンドレスはもうウェイターに現金を渡しています。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: I tell them: No, really, let me pay, but Andrés is already giving cash to the waiter.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Entonces pregunto: ¿Aquí se acostumbra dejar propina?
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: So I ask: Is it customary to leave a tip here?
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: そこで、わたしはたずねます。「ここでは、チップを置く習慣がありますか？」
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: So I ask: Is it customary to leave a tip here?

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Lucía dice que ellos normalmente dejan 10 por ciento si el servicio es bueno.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Lucía says that they usually leave 10 percent if the service is good.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: ルシアは、サービスがよければ、自分たちはふだん10パーセントのチップを置くと言います。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Lucía says that they usually leave 10 percent if the service is good.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Les digo: Si ustedes pagan la cuenta, entonces yo dejo la propina, y ellos aceptan.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: I tell them: If you pay the bill, then I'll leave the tip, and they agree.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 「ふたりがお会計をするなら、わたしがチップを置きます」と言うと、ふたりはそれを受け入れます。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: I tell them: If you pay the bill, then I'll leave the tip, and they agree.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Al final digo: Bueno, gracias, pero la próxima vez invito yo, y todos se ríen.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: At the end I say: OK, thanks, but next time it's on me, and everyone laughs.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 最後に、わたしは言います。「じゃあ、ありがとうございます。でも次は、わたしがおごります。」そして、みんなが笑います。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: At the end I say: OK, thanks, but next time it's on me, and everyone laughs.

speakingGoalInternal: Your new friends insist on paying for breakfast; negotiate politely, accept or decline, and agree how to settle.
speakingGoalJapaneseDraft: 友達と朝食の会計について話し、支払いとチップの分担を丁寧に決めてください。
sourceConflictInternal: The current eight-turn source follows a group breakfast in Oaxaca: narrator offers to pay by card because Lucía and Andrés showed the city; friends insist the narrator is their guest; Andrés gives the waiter cash; Lucía reports they usually leave 10 percent if service was good; narrator offers to leave the tip if friends pay and says next time is on them. The archived generic dialogue replaces this with register-vs-table and staff-check exchanges. Japanese invitation, guest, tip, locale and dictionary senses need qualified review.

reviewQuestionsInternal: The source reports Lucía and Andrés usually leave a 10 percent tip if service is good; this is their stated practice, not an asserted Oaxaca-wide rule.
The waiter brings a table bill/伝票, while the bill-to-pay card uses お会計. Qualified Japanese/dictionary review should settle these contextual senses.

The source guest/invitado is rendered ゲスト, distinct from a café customer. Friends use tú in Spanish; the Japanese deliberately keeps polite learner-facing dialogue and あなた, pending naturalness review.
Pan dulce/sweet bread is rendered 菓子パン without naming a specific Mexican item; qualified food and Japanese review remains open.
Oaxaca, Lucía and Andrés katakana and café waiter terminology require locale/name/register review.
The card payment is only offered, never completed; Andrés is already handing cash to the waiter, with no amount or change added.
The 10 percent figure, if-service-is-good condition, narrator tip offer and next-time treat remain source reported and need contextual dictionary/speaking review.
The archive introduces register-vs-table and ask-staff dialogue absent from current source; no archive row or audio/progress position is imported.
